title: interconnect-memory-bandwidth-long-context-bench
content:
Status: draft notes + initial results (please comment inline)

Goal:
- Understand how host<->GPU interconnect and device memory bandwidth affect tail latency and throughput when serving long-context workloads (>= 4096 tokens) with KV cache enabled.
- Compare A100 / H100 / L40S across common cloud SKU configs and driver/CUDA combinations.
- Surface any non-obvious effects (memory copy stalls, NVLink aggregation behavior, PCIe oversubscription) that show up only with long sequences / large KV caches.

Why this matters (short):
- Our routing/batching heuristics assume per-token cost scales linearly with sequence length; but KV cache access patterns and attention matmuls can change memory pressure and interconnect usage. If interconnect is the bottleneck we should consider: prefix caching on host vs device, pinning heavy contexts to H100/NVLink pools, or adaptive routing.

Summary of experimental design:
- Models: test-model-8B (decoder-only), test-model-70B-ff (larger baseline for sanity).
- Sequence lengths: 2048, 4096, 8192 (primary focus 8192).
- Batch sizes: 1 and 4 (to see microburst vs sustained).
- KV cache mode: on, with repeated stepwise generation to ensure KV cache growth.
- Profiles collected: nvprof / Nsight compute traces (where available), runtime tracing (token timing per-request), OS-level iostat + nvidia-smi sampling, and perf samples on host.
- Cloud SKUs (roughly representative):
  - AWS: p4d.24xlarge (A100, NVLink across 8x GPUs) and p5.24xlarge (H100, NVLink-ish topology)
  - GCP: a2-highgpu-8g (A100, PCIe-heavy, single node NUMA) and t4g-like proxies for L40S (note: L40S availability varies; used partner-provisioned VM)
  - Azure: ND A100 v4 (A100), NDm A100 v4 equivalent (mixed topologies)
- Driver / CUDA combos: CUDA 12.1 + driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.3 + driver 545.xx. We tested both because some kernel paths in cuBLAS/cuDNN/attention kernels change.

Important runtime flags / command snippets (sanity copy):
- rwi serve --model test-model-8B --device gpus --cuda 12.3 --driver 545.40 --batch 1 --max-seq 8192 --kv-cache on --profile=nsight --trace-token-ms 1
- generate loop: python bench_gen.py --length 8192 --tokens-per-step 64 --steps 128 --warmup 10 --concurrency 1

Key findings (high-level):
- For 8192-step runs with KV cache enabled, interconnect topology dominates p99 behavior more than raw TFLOPS for the GPUs we tested. H100 with a strongly connected NVLink mesh had consistently lower p99 (by ~20-35%) vs equivalent A100 machines when NVLink was available.
- When using PCIe-only instances (GCP a2 or some single-socket setups), we observed large p99 spikes at the point KV cache size exceeded device L2 capacity and host<->device transfers increased. These spikes are not visible at 2048 seq lengths.
- L40S performed well for steady-state per-token latency at batch=1 (p50 slightly lower than A100), but showed higher variance under batched generation (batch=4) and worse p99 when driver versions rolled forward (see below). Memory bandwidth per device seems lower than H100 which affects large KV cache reads.
- CUDA/driver combos matter: CUDA 12.3 + driver 545 had improved attention kernel performance on H100 in our samples, but the same combo introduced a regression on some A100 cloud images due to different cuBLAS kernel selection (suspected autotune mismatch).

Representative numbers (aggregated, median of 5 runs, sequence 8192, batch=1, KV on, model test-model-8B):
- H100 (p5-like, NVLink mesh, CUDA12.3/545): p50=18ms/token, p90=28ms/token, p99=55ms/token
- A100 (p4d-like, NVLink less aggregated depending on placement): p50=22ms/token, p90=36ms/token, p99=78ms/token
- A100 (PCIe topology, single-socket): p50=25ms/token, p90=46ms/token, p99=130ms/token (spikes observed during large KV uploads)
- L40S (partner instance, mixed interconnect): p50=20ms/token, p90=40ms/token, p99=95ms/token

Interpretation of numbers:
- p50 differences are modest and track device raw throughput. The larger p99 deltas are correlated with interconnect-induced stalls: when KV cache grows beyond device-resident L2/L3 and requires staged host transfers or peer-to-peer transfers across non-NVLink paths, we observe stalls that amplify tail latency.
- PCIe-only setups occasionally show repeated p99 spikes aligned with periodic memory-manager GC / page pin churn on the host side (observed in iostat and dmesg). This suggests our host-device transfer pattern is not fully pinned/streamed for long-context workloads.

Profiling snippets (highlights):
- Nsight summary on H100: attention kernel time dominated ~45% of token time, but memory copy kernels (HtoD / DtoH) were <10% in NVLink cases.
- On PCIe A100, memory copy kernels rose to ~28% of token time during the phase where KV cache increased beyond 12GB.
- perf samples on host during spike events show heavy off-CPU waits in dma-buf and page fault handling (indicating page-fault-on-demand path for some allocations).

Hypotheses and short experiments to validate:
- Hypothesis A: Tail spikes on PCIe instances are caused by an opportunistic host allocation / copy path that doesn't pre-pin pages for the KV cache when memory pressure is high.
  - Quick test: pre-allocate and mlock KV slab on host, test again.
- Hypothesis B: NVLink aggregation across multiple GPUs reduces effective p99 by enabling peer-to-peer KV reads rather than staged host roundtrips.
  - Quick test: force kernel to use only one GPU (no P2P) on H100 to see delta.
- Hypothesis C: Newer CUDA/driver combinations change kernel-selection heuristics (autotune) and can regress A100; need per-kernel fallback/patch or locked cuBLAS config for A100 fleets.
  - Quick test: run cuBLAS autotune off vs on across drivers and compare microbenchmarks.

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
- For long-context customers, default route to NVLink-equipped instance pools (H100 or A100 NVLink) when sequence length > 4096 and KV cache is enabled. Add a routing policy flag 'prefer-nvlink-for-long-contexts'.
- Implement host-side pre-pinning option for the KV cache allocation path and test across PCIe instances. If pre-pinning eliminates p99 spikes, flip opt-in to default for PCIe fleets.
- Add a runtime check that monitors device L2 consumption vs KV cache growth and emits an SRE alert when host transfers are starting to dominate.
- Create a driver/cuda compatibility matrix for our main SKUs and lock recommended combos in our deployment manifests; include a rollback knob for cuBLAS autotune if regressions are observed.

Longer-term research questions:
- Can we keep large prefixes on host but stream deltas incrementally without producing page-fault churn? Explore RDMA/GPUDirect for host-managed caches.
- Is there an opportunity to compress KV cache entries (quantized keys or lossy sketching) to reduce interconnect pressure for long contexts?
- Better model-aware routing: if a model's KV footprint per token is known, use that to predict per-request interconnect load and route accordingly.

Raw notes / experiment log (chronological snippets):
- 2024-11-15: initial microbench on H100 (NVLink) showed stable p99 ~55ms on 8192 seq; no large spikes across 10k tokens served.
- 2024-11-18: reproduced on A100 p4d with NVLink but p99=78ms, looked ok but placement of model shards across GPUs mattered (same rack vs cross-rack).
- 2024-11-24: ran on GCP a2 single-socket A100; observed periodic 200-500ms spikes correlated with kv-cache growth events; dmesg showed "page allocation failure" warnings intermittently.
- 2024-12-02: tested CUDA 12.1/driver 535 on A100 vs CUDA12.3/545; A100 had better average on 12.1 in our runs but 12.3 improved H100. Flagged INF-1379.

Quick TODOs (owners please):
- Ethan: run pre-pinning experiment across small PCIe fleet and report p99 diff (target by 2024-12-15).
- Sofia: add routing flag in mux for prefer-nvlink-for-long-contexts and wire unit tests (PR stub: linked).
- Luca: prepare a small perf-runner that toggles cuBLAS autotune and collects kernel selection traces for A100/H100 on both driver versions.
- Priya (me): synthesize this doc into a short one-pager for product recommending default pool routing for long-context customers.

Questions for reviewers:
- Do we want to turn pre-pinning on by default for all PCIe fleets or only enable it when KV cache > X GB? Pre-pinning increases host pinned memory usage which can impact co-located workloads.
- How aggressive should routing be to NVLink? If we reserve NVLink capacity for long-contexts we might increase cost for customers who don’t benefit.

Attachments (data pointers):
- Raw nsight traces (s3://redwood-bench/kv-interconnect/2024-11-15/h100-nsight.zip)
- iostat and dmesg logs (s3://redwood-bench/kv-interconnect/2024-11-24/a2-dmesg.tar.gz)
- bench_gen script and run configs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/main/bench/kv-interconnect

Notes to self: keep experiments reproducible and file exact image ids/AMI names in the runsheet. For now this doc captures high-level signal; need deeper kernel-level traces for final RCA.
